trust_decision.summary: A credential id supplied by the caller may only be resolved when the Credential row belongs to the caller's active workspace (or has been explicitly granted to that workspace through a workspace_shared row), and the decision must be made in the service layer before the credential is decrypted or used to build an OpenAI client — decided in packages/server/src/services/openai-assistants-vector-store/index.ts, fed by req.user.activeWorkspaceId from the controller.

landing_point.why: The advisory names openai-assistants-vector-store, and the first thing an engineer reads there is the credential lookup that filters on `id` alone before decrypting the secret and building an OpenAI client.

fix_sites.entry_point: the seven /api/v1/openai-assistants-vector-store routes (workspaceId is taken from req.user and threaded down)
shared guard module (new file packages/server/src/enterprise/utils/tenantRequestGuards.ts) used by the enterprise controllers above
POST /api/v1/document-store/preview and the save/reload path of FILE-STORAGE:: loader paths

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The OAuth2 callback and refresh handlers sit in WHITELIST_URLS because the identity provider's browser redirect carries no session, and the openai-assistants service is the older assistants client while the advisory names the vector-store client, so a solver can argue neither route can or should be workspace-scoped.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A credential explicitly shared into the caller's workspace (a workspace_shared row with itemType 'credential') must stay usable from that workspace, so a bare `findOneBy({ id, workspaceId })` lockout breaks the sharing feature; a guard that also requires req.user.id breaks API-key principals, which authenticate with activeWorkspaceId but no id.

O6_input_shapes: credential id as a query parameter (`?credential=<uuid>`) on the vector-store and assistants routes
credential id as a route parameter (`:id`, `:credentialId`, and the OAuth `state` round-tripped back to /callback)
credential owned directly by the caller's workspace versus granted in through a workspace_shared row
caller principal shape: interactive session with req.user.id versus API-key caller with activeWorkspaceId but no id
multi-id arrays (body.ids deduped and filtered to non-empty strings) and optional body fields (storeId) alongside single ids

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/v1/openai-assistants?credential=<uuid> — resolves any credential by id and lists that OpenAI account's assistants
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is the older assistants client, not the vector-store client the advisory names, and the route only has assistants:view
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate service module one directory over; not imported by anything the report mentions

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /api/v1/openai-assistants/:id?credential=<uuid> — resolves any credential by id and retrieves/expands an assistant
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: same legacy assistants client; appears to be a read-only viewer helper

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/v1/openai-assistants-file/upload/?credential=<uuid> — uploads files into another workspace's OpenAI account with its key
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The mount has no assistants permission middleware, so it looks like an internal/legacy helper rather than a supported API
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different route mount (openai-assistants-files) and controller method

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/v1/oauth2-credential/callback — whitelisted, unauthenticated; `state` is used directly as the credential id and the victim credential's clientSecret is spent against its token endpoint
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The provider redirect cannot carry a session, and the handler's own comment says state is assumed to be the credential id
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the fixed /authorize handler, different handler

O8_uncovered_routes.route: POST /api/v1/oauth2-credential/refresh/:credentialId — whitelisted, unauthenticated; returns the refreshed tokenInfo (including access_token) for any credential id
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Token refresh is listed in WHITELIST_URLS and takes no user, so it looks unreachable from a tenant-scoped session check
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~230 lines below the fixed handler

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second credential-to-OpenAI-client helper used by the file-upload path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer hardening the vector-store client would plausibly leave the deprecated assistants client alone, and the upload path was written separately with its own credential lookup.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A workspace-scoped credential resolver that other services are expected to call
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The correct pattern already lives here; a maintainer refactoring IDOR fixes often adds one shared resolver and converts only some call sites.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third OAuth2 handler resolving the credential from a caller-supplied id
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The refresh endpoint was added after the authorize flow, so the same scoping rule is easy to forget on the newer handler.

O9_family: Improper authorization / broken tenant isolation (IDOR, CWE-285/CWE-863/CWE-639) on credential objects

O10_build.toolchain: pnpm workspace + turbo monorepo; tsc build with gulp; jest via ts-jest; typeorm migrations
services: outbound HTTPS to api.openai.com for the allow path only
O10_build.project_tests: jest unit tests under packages/server/src (**/*.test.ts) that mock repositories/services; there are no pre-existing tests for openai-assistants, openai-assistants-vector-store or the oauth2 routes, and the fix adds only packages/server/src/enterprise/utils/tenantRequestGuards.test.ts

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add `workspaceId: req.user.activeWorkspaceId` to each Credential findOneBy in the vector-store service only, copying the existing getCredentialById pattern, which locks out workspace-shared credentials and leaves the assistants and oauth2 routes open.

out_of_scope_notes: The same commit also hardens chatflow, upsert-history, lead, dataset, evaluation and document-store scoping in this repository; those are separate protections and were not assessed beyond noting they are part of the same published fix.
